{{Short description|Method to avoid singularities in classical mechanics}}
In [[mathematical physics]], the '''Kustaanheimo–Stiefel regularization''' is a method to transform the spatial [[Kepler problem]] into a spatial harmonic oscillator using the '''Kustaanheimo–Stiefel (regularization) map'''. Both are named after [[Paul Kustaanheimo]] and [[Eduard Stiefel]], who introduced them in 1965. Simply put, the idea is to increase the dimension to untangle [[Singularity (mathematics)|singularities]] arising from collisions.

== Kustaanheimo–Stiefel map ==
The Kustaanheimo–Stiefel map is an extension of the complex [[Hopf fibration]] <math>h_\mathbb{C}\colon S^3\rightarrow S^2</math>, using complex and [[complex projective space]] given by <math>h_\mathbb{C}\colon\mathbb{C}^2\supset S^3\rightarrow S^2\cong\mathbb{C}P^1,
(z,w)\mapsto[z:w]</math>, by a squared radial component. It is a map <math>\Phi\colon\mathbb{R}^4\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^3</math> given by filling with <math>0\mapsto 0</math> of the map:

: <math>
h_\mathbb{C}\times-^2\colon
\mathbb{R}^4
\cong S^3\times\mathbb{R}^+\rightarrow S^2\times\mathbb{R}^+
\cong\mathbb{R}^3.
</math>

In [[cartesian coordinates]], the Kustaanheimo–Stiefel map <math>\mathbb{R}^4\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^3,
(x,y,z,w)\mapsto(a,b,c)</math> is given by:<ref>Waldvogel 2010, Eq. (32)</ref>

: <math>
a=x^2-y^2-z^2+w^2;
</math>
: <math>
b=2(xy-zw);
</math>
: <math>
c=2(xz+yw).
</math>

The above squaring of the distance, hence a<math>
a^2+b^2+c^2=(x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2)^2
</math>, follows from the [[Binomial formula|binomial formulas]].
